95.0.0.en: 1- O come, let us sing unto the LORD: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation. 2- Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms.

95.0.1.en: 1- No one can sing but the penitent. So here is a call to the penitent who believe in God to sing to Him; indeed, to lift up their voices in praise and thanksgiving with a joyful shout, because He has offered a mighty salvation, firm like a rock, and has offered it to the whole world. He alone is the Savior of the world, and this is a clear prophecy of the Incarnation of Christ, the Redeemer of mankind.

95.0.2.en: 2- The joyful shout means inward faith and a raised voice to call those who are far off. So this verse is a call from the believers to the unbelievers to believe and share in singing and praising God the Savior. This sharing is in a spiritual joy, not like the passing joys of the world.

95.0.3.en: 3- Singing to the Lord and the joyful shout, that is, praise in a loud voice to God our Savior, surely gladdens our hearts and affects those around us. It draws them to thanksgiving, singing and sharing in the joy, as happens in the feasts of the Church in which we praise God, and the feasts of the saints, in which we come before God with praise and hymns and cry out, not only with our voices but with our hearts rejoicing.

95.1.0.en: 3- For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods.

95.1.1.en: 1- In glorifying God, the psalmist declares that God is a great God, not like the pagan Gentiles, these weak gods. He is higher than all gods, and spiritual, whereas the gods of the Gentiles are demons that incline to sins and base lusts.

95.1.2.en: 2- The Lord is a great King above all gods, and these gods are:

95.1.3.en: a- The angels in all their ranks, including principalities, powers and lords.

95.1.4.en: b- The rulers and kings of the world.

95.1.5.en: c- The Gentiles and their pagan gods, which they claim are gods although they are demons.

95.1.6.en: So the Lord is a King who reigns over all these forms of power and authority, because He is greater than all.

95.2.0.en: 4- In his hand are the deep places of the earth: the strength of the hills is his also. 5- The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land.

95.2.1.en: “The deep places of the earth”: the deep parts of the earth.

95.2.2.en: “His hands formed”: made and shaped it, as metals are shaped after being heated.

95.2.3.en: 1- God has authority to know everything in the depths of the earth, and also all the treasures hidden in the mountains, and He made the great sea that carries mighty ships and overturns them if He wills. God is also the maker of the earth on which man lives, which rises between the seas and oceans.

95.2.4.en: 2- God knows everyone who strives toward the depth while he lives on the earth, and everyone who strives to acquire the treasures of the mountains when he goes up on them and struggles spiritually in solitude, prayers and meditations, seeking spiritual elevation. He knows all that is in the earth and the sea; that is, all secrets are open before Him, even if a man were to rise above the mountain peaks or hide in the belly of the seas. This shows the greatness of God and His knowledge of everything, and therefore all mankind must submit to Him and offer Him glory.

95.2.5.en: How beautiful it is to contemplate God and His greatness, so that we glorify Him and praise Him, for praising Him fills the heart with joy and spreads joy to all who are around.

95.3.0.en: 6- O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the LORD our maker. 7- For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice, 8- Harden not your heart, as in the provocation, and as in the day of temptation in the wilderness. “Let us kneel”: let us bow down and bend.

95.3.1.en: “Massah” is a word meaning trial, and “Meribah” is a word meaning contention. The two words recall a place at the beginning of the journey of the children of Israel, in Rephidim, an area in western Sinai (Ex 17:7). Then Meribah is mentioned again at the end of the journey at Kadesh-barnea, which lies east of Sinai and south of the land of Canaan (Num 20:13). In these two places the people murmured against God and fell into doubt, so God was angry with them and with Moses and Aaron

95.3.2.en: 1- In the joy of exultation and praise, the psalmist calls for submission before God, and he expresses this submission by bowing down, kneeling and bending before Him. For He alone is our Creator, so submission, worship and glorification are due to Him; and He is also our Shepherd and we are His sheep, who follow Him and submit to Him and find in Him their salvation and life. He has prepared for them pasture, water and rest, for He is responsible for them, so they are bound to Him and submit to Him at all times lest they go astray.

95.3.3.en: 2- Prostration, with kneeling and touching the ground, is a man’s declaration before God of his weakness and the multitude of his sins, and an offering of repentance for them. Then he rises and stands upright to glorify God, who forgives his sins, and to praise Him and glorify Him for all His blessings.

95.3.4.en: 3- After speaking of the greatness of God and the necessity of glorifying Him and submitting to Him, the psalmist warns the people of God not to murmur against Him or refuse to obey Him, as happened of old at Meribah and Massah, because the people of old were hard of heart. But “today” means the present span of man’s life and his life on earth, in which submission to God and obedience to Him are required.

95.4.0.en: 9- When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my work. 10- Forty years long was I grieved with that generation, and said, It is a people that do err in their heart, and they have not known my ways. 11- So I sware in my wrath that they should not enter into my rest.

95.4.1.en: 1- God gave very great care to His people in the wilderness of Sinai. Despite the harshness of conditions in that wilderness, God gave them, in a miraculous way, food and drink, led them by the pillar of fire and the cloud, preserved their clothes and sandals for forty years, and protected them from all the tribes hostile to them. But they refused to obey Him, and strayed from Him in their hearts and minds, and refused to enter the Promised Land, the land of Canaan, so God deprived them of it.

95.4.2.en: 2- Everyone who now murmurs against God and does not obey His commandments, God deprives of His rest, that is, eternal life.

95.4.3.en: Hold fast to God’s commandments and obey His word, even if it seems hard. Trust that He will support you and help you to carry out His commandments; indeed, your heart will delight in His fellowship, and then in the end you will rejoice with an inexpressible joy in the eternal Kingdom.

95.4.4.en: A call to glorify God: “O sing unto the LORD a new song … v. 1”

95.4.6.en: 1- Its author: there are two opinions:

95.4.7.en: a- It has no title in the Beirut edition, so it is considered one of the orphan psalms, that is, those whose author is unknown.

95.4.8.en: b- David the prophet, according to what the Septuagint states.

95.4.9.en: 2- When was it written? There are opinions:

95.4.10.en: a- When the ark of the covenant of God was brought back from the house of Obed-edom the Gittite to Jerusalem (1 Chr 16:23-33).

95.4.11.en: b- A prophecy of the glorification of God in the Temple that Solomon would build.

95.4.12.en: c- A prophecy of the praise of God and the offering of sacrifices to Him after the building of the Temple by Zerubbabel, that is, after the return from the captivity, as the title of this psalm in the Septuagint states.

95.4.13.en: 3- This psalm is a call to mankind to glorify God, not the Jews only but the Gentiles also. This was not clearly fulfilled until the New Testament.

95.4.14.en: 4- This psalm is considered a call to glorify God in the heart of man. And the heart of man is also a temple of the Holy Spirit. So it is the return of the penitent man to God and the glorification of His holy name.

95.4.15.en: 5- This psalm is a call to the Church of the New Testament to praise God alone and not be occupied with the cares of the world, which are the many gods.

95.4.16.en: 6- This psalm is one of the royal psalms, which begin with Psalm 95 and run to Psalm 100, in addition to Psalm 93, which is an introduction to them.

95.4.17.en: 7- This psalm is found in the Agpeya at the beginning of the prayer of the Ninth Hour, in which Christ completed the redemption of mankind and died for it; therefore the whole earth glorifies Him, because He alone is its Savior.

96.0.0.en: 1- O sing unto the LORD a new song: sing unto the LORD, all the earth.

96.0.1.en: 1- David the prophet calls the Jews and the Gentiles, that is, all the earth, to praise God, for with the eye of prophecy he sees Christ the Savior, who redeems mankind, so that all the earth praises Him.

96.0.2.en: 2- The praise of God is a new praise, that is, in spirit and in truth, where we rise above the lusts and the old man and praise in the Spirit. This is the praise of the Church, which she began after the Resurrection of Christ and the descent of the Holy Spirit, and this praise is the joy with which she has evangelized the whole world.

96.1.0.en: 2- Sing unto the LORD, bless his name; shew forth his salvation from day to day.

96.1.1.en: 1- The psalm calls us to sing and bless the name of the Lord, because the name of the Lord is great, and He is the One who arranged salvation for His people in the Old Testament and completed His redemption in the New Testament; therefore calling on the name of Christ is a powerful prayer that protects His children and overcomes the demons.

96.1.2.en: 2- Proclaiming the salvation of Christ is the aim of believers who praise God, through their lived life and through every word that comes out of their mouths, “from day to day”; that is, the Old and the New Testament, and it also means constant proclamation throughout life.

96.2.0.en: 3- Declare his glory among the heathen, his wonders among all people.

96.2.1.en: 1- The psalm calls the believers to speak of the glory of God and not of their own glory; that is, the servant hides himself and shows Christ, and the proclamation of Christ is to every person, for it says “among the heathen”; that is, the speaking is not limited to the Jews but includes the whole world.

96.2.2.en: 2- Speaking of the wonders of God means His great works that He did with mankind, the summit of which is His Incarnation from a virgin without the seed of man, to redeem mankind. And the works of God are wonders that take place every day to draw souls to Him and to do all that helps them to live with Him.

96.3.0.en: 4- For the LORD is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods.

96.3.1.en: This verse mentions three attributes of God that distinguish Him from the rest of the pagan gods and from all the powers of the world that exist to this day. These attributes are:

96.3.2.en: 1- “Great”: that is, all perfection is in Him, and He is exalted above everything man knows.

96.3.3.en: 2- “Greatly to be praised”: that is, He is worthy of praise and glory at all times, because there is none like Him in all the earth.

96.3.4.en: 3- “To be feared”: that is, fearful, because He is able to do all things and no one can stand before Him, and in His hand is the life of all people, and He has authority of judgment.

96.4.0.en: 5- For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the LORD made the heavens.

96.4.1.en: Here the psalmist declares the truth about those called gods among the Gentiles. There are, of course, no gods other than God, but these gods are demons that deceive people with their false power so that they worship them, yet these demons have no power before God. The true God is the only God who created everything in the world, and created the heavens and created in them the angels, some of whom fell, and these are the demons. So He is the Creator of the demons, and how can they stand before Him?!

96.5.0.en: 6- Glory and majesty are before him: strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.

96.5.1.en: 1- He continues to describe God, saying that glory and majesty, that is, greatness and splendor, go before Him to prepare His way, and those who prepare His way are the angels, the prophets, the Apostles, and all the priests and servants of the New Testament. These are clothed in righteousness and declare the glory of God by their lives and their teachings.

96.5.2.en: 2- But in the sanctuary of God, that is, His place (for since He is holy, His place is holy), we find strength and beauty in it. Strength is blessing and goodness, and in it are all the treasures of knowledge and love. Beauty means all the perfections of God, and it is unlimited, and everyone who enters into it in a relationship of love is satisfied and rejoices. These are God’s gifts to those who believe in Him, who love Him.

96.5.3.en: How beautiful it is to contemplate the attributes of God and to praise His holy name, for it fills the heart with joy, keeps sin away from man, and fills him with love of good for every person.

96.6.s.en: (2) The worship of the Lord is fear and joy

96.6.0.en: 7- Give unto the LORD, O ye kindreds of the people, give unto the LORD glory and strength.

96.6.1.en: The psalmist calls the Gentiles, that is, the unbelievers, to believe in God and give Him glory and honor, because He deserves glorification, and to Him all power is ascribed. And if a man believes in Him, all the powers and glories of the world become small before him.

96.7.0.en: 8- Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name: bring an offering, and come into his courts.

96.7.1.en: He adds also, in the worship of God, that the Gentiles should repeat the holy name of God and glorify Him, for His great name crushes all the power of Satan. Then, as man’s love for God grows through many prayers, he offers Him offerings in His holy Temple, whether in the Temple of the Old Testament among the Jews, or in the courts of the Lord, that is, the churches of the New Testament. The offerings are not sacrifices but the good works that we add to the divine praises. Thus we see from (vv. 7, 8) a clear prophecy of the faith of the Gentiles and their offering of worship to God, and this is what was fulfilled in the Church of the New Testament.

96.8.0.en: 9- O worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness: fear before him, all the earth.

96.8.1.en: 1- The psalmist continues his speech about the worship of God and asks those who believe in Him to worship Him in submission, represented by prostration before Him in His house. He sets a condition for worship, that it be in holy adornment, and this means the following:

96.8.2.en: a- We wear modest clothes that befit reverence before God in His house.

96.8.3.en: b- We adorn ourselves with spiritual virtues.

96.8.4.en: 2- He demands that the inhabitants of the earth, that is, all people, fear God and tremble before Him, so that they leave the worship of idols and all their sins and come forward in faith and purity to worship Him, just as the heavenly angels cover their faces and their feet before God the awesome when they stand before Him and praise Him.

96.9.0.en: 10- Say among the heathen that the LORD reigneth: the world also shall be established that it shall not be moved: he shall judge the people righteously.

96.9.1.en: 1- The psalmist proclaims to the Gentiles that the Lord has reigned, and in the Septuagint “reigned from the tree”; that is, the crucified Christ is the Redeemer of mankind. So he proclaims to them salvation from sin and enjoyment of fellowship with God. Then they live in assurance in His churches spread throughout the world, which establish the believers in the whole inhabited earth. For the world is established by the salvation offered in the churches of the New Testament.

96.9.2.en: 2- Whoever does not believe in God and persists in his sins has nothing before him but the judgment that Christ will carry out at His second coming, when He will judge and destroy the wicked, and at the same time glorify His children who believe in Him and are firm in His commandments.

96.10.0.en: 11- Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad; let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof.

96.10.1.en: “Let roar”: the roaring is the sound of crashing waters, and it is a loud sound.

96.10.2.en: 1- The psalmist calls the heaven to rejoice; that is, he calls all the angels to rejoice in the salvation of God which He offers on the Cross to mankind. Then he returns and calls the earth also to be glad in this salvation that it receives in the Church by the Holy Spirit, and so heaven and earth share in joy in the salvation of God. And as the angels came down to earth with joy to proclaim Christ, so also the righteous went up to heaven to see its glories, like Paul and John the Seer.

96.10.3.en: 2- The sea is a symbol of the world, and by it is meant all the Gentiles, and he calls them too to rejoice and to declare this with sounds of joy, symbolized by the crashing of its waves, that is, their clapping and praise. For the Gentiles share in the Church of the New Testament in the worship and glorification of God.

96.11.0.en: 12- Let the field be joyful, and all that is therein: then shall all the trees of the wood rejoice 13- Before the LORD: for he cometh, for he cometh to judge the earth: he shall judge the world with righteousness, and the people with his truth. “Be joyful”: be glad.

96.11.1.en: “The wood” (literally, rugged places): difficult places; the trees of the wood mean the Gentiles.

96.11.2.en: 1- The psalmist calls the plants of the field, that is, the land that the farmer tends, to grow and bear fruit and so rejoice in their fruits, and by the plants of the field he means the Jews, whom God cared for as His own special people that they might grow in faith. In addition to the Jews, he also calls the trees of the wood, which are unfruitful trees, to bear fruit too by the power of God. By the trees of the wood are meant the Gentiles who believe in Christ and so bear spiritual fruits. Thus the whole world, Jews and Gentiles, rejoices in the salvation of Christ.

96.11.3.en: 2- This joy is lived by the believers before God, and they enjoy His coming in the fullness of time, that is, His Incarnation and His death on the Cross, which condemned sin and freed His children from its bondage that they might rejoice with Him. Then he repeats the word “judge,” saying He shall judge the world with righteousness, and this will be fulfilled at His second coming on the last day of judgment, when the evil of the wicked will appear and they will be punished with perdition, because they saw God’s faithfulness toward them in His care for them and His call to them to believe, and also His faithfulness that appeared in the lives of His children who lived among them. And these children of His, who believe in Him, He glorifies in His Kingdom at the same time that He punishes the wicked.

96.11.4.en: This life is an opportunity to worship God and walk in good works, so our hearts rejoice in His fellowship, and then complete eternal joy awaits us in the Kingdom of Heaven.

96.11.5.en: The Lord, the great King: “The LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice; let the multitude of isles be glad thereof … v. 1”

96.11.7.en: 1- Its author: there are two opinions:

96.11.8.en: a- There is no title for this psalm, and consequently it is considered one of the orphan psalms, that is, those whose author is unknown.

96.11.9.en: b- In the Septuagint it is stated that its author is David the prophet.

96.11.10.en: 2- When was it written? The Septuagint states in the title of this psalm that it is “of David, when his land was restored to him,” that is, when David triumphed over all his enemies, and the land submitted to him and paid him tribute, and he rested from his wars, and that was at the end of his life.

96.11.11.en: 3- This psalm is also among the group of royal psalms that speak of the Lord the King, and they are the psalms from (Ps 95 - Ps 100), in addition to Psalm 93, which prepares the way for them.

96.11.12.en: 4- This psalm is considered one of the messianic psalms that prophesy about Christ the awaited Messiah, who reigned from the tree, which is the Cross, and bound Satan, and the earth was restored to Him, that is, the believers in Him, and He raised them from hell to paradise.

96.11.13.en: 5- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Ninth Hour, in which Christ reigned on the Cross, condemned Satan, and gave joy to His children who believe in Him, who were in hell, and raised them to paradise.
